verdict.reason: Y translates all content including the page number and first formula while accurately resolving OCR artifacts, whereas X omits the first formula and page number and invents a 'Wind-Harmonizing' formula category from misread text.

X faithfully translates marginal source attributions and correctly resolves OCR errors in formula numbering, whereas Y omits the source marker '丹', mistakes formula number 179 for a page number, and replaces the character '偏' with an obscured text notice.

Translation X correctly recognizes that author attributions follow each poem, whereas Translation Y treats them as prefixes, systematically misattributing every poem, omitting Shi Ping, and failing to connect Su Shi to his verse.
Translation X faithfully translates the text on the page, whereas Translation Y adds an extraneous continuation clause not present in the source that leaves the opening sentence as a fragment.
Y faithfully includes the opening characters and translates all formula numbers accurately, whereas X omits the opening characters and misreads numbers 2 and 1 as 21 and 10.

Translation X correctly identifies and reads the bronze vessel and inscription as "Li" and faithfully translates the inscription comparison, whereas Translation Y misreads "鬲" as "Ge", misinterprets the inscription note as a statement about terminology, and converts Chinese units directly into English inches and ounces.

X accurately renders the classical syntax and exegesis, whereas Y misattributes the opening lacuna theory, omits the king sending to stop Zixi (止子西), and mistranslates the final phrase 自正 as 'From the perspective of...'.
Translation X correctly recognizes that the page begins and ends mid-sentence, whereas Translation Y mistranslates '刻見效' as 'clearly observed' and fabricates the object 'Qi' at the end.
X accurately preserves the original Chinese units of measurement and structural markup tags, whereas Y translates traditional units directly into English feet and inches.

Y correctly identifies marginal OCR artifacts and accurately translates key Song bureaucratic titles such as Yitong Sansi and Pingzhang, whereas X mistranslates these central official titles and mechanically renders stray characters as body text.

X faithfully preserves the text's parallel calendrical arguments and technical terminology, whereas Y distorts '皆指歲言' as pointing to the start of an era and anachronistically renders '時刻' as 'modern moments'.
X faithfully preserves the original Chinese measurement units rather than inaccurately converting them to Western inches and feet, and renders the title without adding extraneous words.
X correctly identifies the OCR error of 金草 for 金革 (military affairs) and translates 乙亥 as a day rather than a year, whereas Y mistakenly interprets 金草 as 'gold and grass' and translates 乙亥 as a year.

Translation Y faithfully preserves the page's incomplete sentence structure by translating the trailing conjunction '而' as 'and' and accounts for the marginal characters and OCR error, whereas Translation X artificially closes the final sentence by dropping '而' and ignores the marginal characters.
Translation X faithfully translates this Zhouyi commentary on the Meng hexagram, whereas Translation Y is completely unrelated text concerning Song Dynasty official rank reforms.
Translation X is complete and correctly identifies the commentator attributions '伊' and '房' as well as the page number, whereas Translation Y omits them entirely.
Translation Y is a faithful and complete translation of the classical poems and excerpts on rain, whereas Translation X is an entirely unrelated text concerning herbal medicine formulas.

X correctly recognizes that the OCR-split numerals '十' and '九' represent formula 19 for Zhenyuan Yin and accurately renders Weiguan Jian as a decoction, whereas Y misidentifies the formula number as 10, creates an erroneous page 19 tag, and mistranslates the decoction as a bolus.

Translation X accurately identifies the recipe as a continuation from the previous page while faithfully noting illegible quantities, whereas Translation Y misattributes the formula to the Great Aloe Pill and invents dosages for licorice and poria that are not in the source text.
Y correctly identifies the opening header as an OCR misreading of the Siku Quanshu rather than mistranslating it as a book about Venus, and also translates '右' which X omits.

X correctly interprets the cataloguing formula '右' as referring to the preceding vessel and preserves traditional Chinese measurement units with glosses, whereas Y mistranslates '右' literally as 'To the right:' and inaccurately converts decimal Chinese units into feet and inches.

Y is more faithful because it accurately translates the commentary and natural attributes (such as rendering '雷疾' as 'thunder is swift' rather than 'thunder strikes' and capturing '莫有使之然者' without interpolating 'external force'), whereas X contains several mistranslations and factual errors.
